answer.rationale: The two live symptoms — onboarding completion down 4% and activation down 6% — are causally linked, and onboarding sits upstream of activation, so fixing the funnel entry has the best chance of moving both. Inherited memory supports this from two independent angles (memory_86 on onboarding shortening, memory_31 on signup simplification), and both describe durable rather than headline-only lifts. I am deliberately NOT choosing promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 records exactly that move producing a 31% conversion and 18% revenue spike while costing 12 points of later-cycle retention, and it carries an explicit instruction not to treat it as a repeatable win. Matching a price war would trade sustainable qualified revenue for a short-term number, which is the opposite of the stated objective. referral_incentive (memory_57) is sound but targets established customers, not the segment where the bleeding is; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is real but addresses a different funnel than the one degrading. I am spending verification on memory_86 because it is the direct basis for the action and its summary lacks effect size, segment definition, and any retention/quality follow-through — precisely the gap that made memory_73 misleading before it was corrected. I am spending the second pull on memory_91 because activation_messaging is the strongest competing direction and its summary is the vaguest of the set ('improved engagement', 'nudged more accounts') with no magnitude and no durability window; if the archive shows a large, durable, cheap effect there, I will switch. Residual uncertainty I am not resolving: none of these memories were measured under competitive price pressure, so the baseline they were established against no longer holds, and a self-serve funnel improvement may be partly offset by accounts leaving on price regardless. Downstream risk flagged: stripping onboarding or signup steps can raise completion while lowering lead qualification and data quality, i.e. more accounts through the door that are worth less — the same shape of failure as memory_73. So the experiment must carry qualified-revenue and retention guardrails alongside the completion metric, and be read at a later checkpoint, not at the completion spike. Standard experiment scale rather than broad rollout, since the supporting evidence is summary-level and unverified at the time of writing.
